cars.specification_market: Museo Nicolis collection-listed 1928 CGSS, used as a documented road-sporting reference for the original CGS/CGSS family. Eight attributes follow the Italian museum record, corroborated against its English translation. Retain 37 CV from the Italian table/text; do not silently relabel as brake horsepower because English narrative says hp. No power standard/rpm, torque, aspiration, exact gearbox/differential fitment, weight, wheelbase, or timed speed inferred. Later four-speed/differential statement is not attached to this particular car. Louwman historical exhibition supplies context only, not a 350-kg tax-class eligibility or race-result claim for the CGSS. Photo represents another labelled 1927 CGSS open body; not proof of the Nicolis 1928 car, Duval coachbuilder, engine or original equipment. Related CGS/CGSS road versions count once; no dedicated C6/racing car, replica or extra body/version admission.
cars.summary: The Amilcar CGS/CGSS belongs to the interwar lightweight sporting-road tradition. Its lowered CGSS chassis, uprated small engine and enlarged drum brakes supported a model popular with gentleman drivers entering competitions, as documented by Museo Nicolis. Count the related CGS/CGSS road family once, without adding coachbuilders or individual chassis.

facts.title: CGSS is an evolution, not another count
facts.explanation: Museo Nicolis describes CGSS as the sporting development of CGS, with a lower chassis and engine/brake improvements. The archive groups both related road stages once rather than multiplying the name, body or individual car.
